summary: 意大利长期将疟疾归因于坏空气或遗传，确认蚊虫传播后才得以有组织地防治。文章追踪奎宁发放、战争造成的反复与战后公共卫生行动，说明全国行动也须顾及各地条件。

paragraphs.brief: 意大利语中的“疟疾”一词的意思是“坏空气”，这一可怕的疾病标志着该国数千年来人民的生活。
sentences: The word ‘malaria’ means ‘bad air’ in Italian, and this terrible disease marked the life of the people of that country for thousands of years.
意大利语中的“疟疾”一词的意思是“坏空气”，这一可怕的疾病标志着该国数千年来人民的生活。
Yet by 1962, Italy was officially declared malaria-free, and it has remained so ever since.
然而，到1962年，意大利被正式宣布为无疟疾国家，自那以后一直如此。
Frank Snowden’s study of this successful endeavour is a remarkable piece of historical work.
Frank Snowden对这项成功工作的研究是一份了不起的历史著作。
Original, crystal clear, analytical and passionate, Snowden takes us to areas historians have rarely visited before.
斯诺登带我们去历史学家们很少去过的地方。

paragraphs.brief: 这些理论的后果是，在该世纪结束之前，在防治这一疾病方面没有做多少工作。
sentences: Everybody now knows that malaria is carried by mosquitoes.
现在人人都知道，疟疾是由蚊子携带的。
But in the 19th century most experts subscribed to the theory of ‘miasma’ or ‘poisoning of the air’.
但19世纪，大多数专家都赞同“弥撒”或“毒气”理论。
Others made a link between swamps, water and malaria, but did not make the further leap towards insects.
另一些则在沼泽地、水和疟疾之间建立联系，但没有进一步向昆虫过渡。
The consequence of these theories was that little was done to combat the disease before the end of that century.
这些理论的后果是，在该世纪结束之前，在防治这一疾病方面没有做多少工作。
The situation was so serious that from a total population of 25m Italians, 11m were ‘permanently at risk’.
情况如此严重，在2 500万意大利人中，有11万人 " 永远处于危险之中 "。
In warm, damp, malarial zones, the life expectancy of land workers was a terrifying 22.5 years.
在温暖、潮湿、疟疾地区，土地工人的预期寿命是可怕的22.5岁。
The economic impact of the disease was immense.
该疾病的经济影响是巨大的。
Epidemics were blamed on people who originated from the hotter parts of Italy, given the widespread belief that malaria was hereditary.
流行病归咎于来自意大利更热的地区的人，因为人们普遍认为疟疾是遗传的。

paragraphs.brief: 1898年，防治疟疾战争取得的第一个突破是，动物学家Giovanni Battista Grassi证明，造成这一疾病的微生物是在蚊子的消化道中携带的。
sentences: One of the first breakthroughs in the war against malaria came in 1898 when the zoologist Giovanni Battista Grassi demonstrated that the micro-organisms causing the disease were carried in the digestive tract of the mosquito.
1898年，防治疟疾战争取得的第一个突破是，动物学家Giovanni Battista Grassi证明，造成这一疾病的微生物是在蚊子的消化道中携带的。
By releasing mosquitoes into rooms to drink the blood of healthy human volunteers, Grassi was able to make the direct link between the insects and the disease.
Grassi把蚊子放进房间喝人体健康志愿者的血，使昆虫和疾病直接联系起来。

Definitive proof of this theory was obtained after an extraordinary series of experiments in Italy, where healthy people were introduced into malarial zones but kept free of mosquito bites – and remained well.
在意大利进行了一系列非同寻常的实验，使健康的人进入疟疾地区，但没有蚊子咬到，并且保持良好。
The recently formed Italian state at last had the necessary information to begin tackling the disease.
最近成立的意大利国家终于掌握了必要的信息来开始应对这一疾病。

paragraphs.brief: 采用了一种复杂的方法，使用奎宁——一种从树皮中获取的药物，长期以来一直用于防治发烧，但现在却被视为防治疟疾战争的一个关键部分。
sentences: A complicated approach was adopted, which made use of quinine – a drug obtained from tree bark which had long been used to combat fever, but was now seen as a crucial part of the war on malaria.
采用了一种复杂的方法，使用奎宁——一种从树皮中获取的药物，长期以来一直用于防治发烧，但现在却被视为防治疟疾战争的一个关键部分。
Italy introduced a quinine law and a quinine tax in 1904, and the drug was administered to large numbers of rural workers.
意大利于1904年实行奎宁法和奎宁税，向大量农村工人发放了该药。
Despite its often terrible side effects, the drug was successful in limiting the spread of the disease, and in breaking cycles of infection.
尽管这种药物往往产生可怕的副作用，但它成功地限制了疾病的传播，打破了感染的循环。
In addition, Italy set up rural health centres and invested heavily in education programmes.
此外，意大利还建立了农村保健中心，对教育方案进行了大量投资。
Malaria, as Snowden shows, was not just a medical problem, but a social and regional issue, and could only be defeated through multi-layered strategies.
正如斯诺登所显示的，疟疾不仅是一个医疗问题，也是一个社会和区域问题，只有通过多层次的战略才能战胜。

paragraphs.brief: 但是尽管遭到拒绝，整个战略还是取得了巨大成功。
sentences: It was originally decided to give quinine to all those in vulnerable regions – even healthy people.
最初决定给脆弱地区的所有人-甚至健康的人-奎宁。
However, peasants were often suspicious of medicine being forced upon them, and doctors were frequently met with hostility and stubborn refusal to accept the treatment offered.
然而，农民往往怀疑他们被强迫服用药物，医生经常受到敌视和顽固拒绝接受所提供的治疗。
But despite the refusals, the strategy as a whole was hugely successful.
但是尽管遭到拒绝，整个战略还是取得了巨大成功。
Deaths from malaria fell by some 80% in the first decade of the 20th century and some areas escaped altogether from the scourge of the disease.
20世纪头十年，疟疾造成的死亡人数下降了约80%，一些地区完全摆脱了疟疾的祸害。

paragraphs.brief: 1915-18年的战争推迟了这场运动，因为资金被转移到战场上。
sentences: The 1915-18 war delayed the campaign, as funds were diverted to the battlefields.
1915-18年的战争推迟了这场运动，因为资金被转移到战场上。
In the 1920s and 1930s the draining of the damp, unhealthy marshlands around Rome had a certain impact on the spread of malaria.
1920年代和1930年代，罗马周围潮湿、不健康的沼泽地排水，对疟疾蔓延产生了一定影响。
However, as war swept through the drained lands in the 1940s, the disease returned with a vengeance.
然而，随着战争在1940年代席卷了贫瘠的土地，这一疾病又以复仇回升。
Yet the country’s leading malariologist Alberto Missiroli refused to order the distribution of quinine, so allowing the epidemic to spread unchecked.
然而，该国首席疟疾专家阿尔贝托·米西罗利拒绝下令分发奎宁，任由疫情蔓延。

According to Snowden, he did this in order to create the ideal conditions for a new strategy, supported by the US Rockefeller Foundation – a massive experiment involving the extermination of mosquitoes with the chemical DDT.
根据斯诺登的说法，他这样做是为了为一项得到美国洛克菲勒基金会支持的新战略创造理想的条件，这是一项涉及用滴滴涕消灭蚊子的大规模实验。
It is estimated that more than a third of the inhabitants in the affected area contracted malaria and countless thousands died.
据估计，受灾地区三分之一以上的居民感染了疟疾，成千上万人死亡。

paragraphs.brief: 随着1945年战争的结束，美国政府和洛克菲勒基金会可以自由地进行试验。
sentences: With the end of the war in 1945, the US government and the Rockefeller Foundation were free to experiment.
随着1945年战争的结束，美国政府和洛克菲勒基金会可以自由地进行试验。
DDT was sprayed from the air, and 3m Italians had their bodies covered with the chemical.
滴滴涕是从空中喷洒的，3m意大利人的身体被该化学品覆盖。
The effects were immense, and by 1962 malaria was more or less gone from the whole country.
其影响是巨大的，到1962年，疟疾或多或少从全国消失。
One of the final victims to die of the disease in Italy was the popular cyclist, Fausto Coppi.
意大利最后死于这一疾病的受害者之一是流行的骑自行车者Fausto Coppi。
He had contracted malaria in Africa in 1960, and the failure of doctors in Italy to spot the disease was a sign of the times.
他于1960年在非洲感染了疟疾，意大利的医生未能发现这一疾病是时代的一个标志。
A few decades earlier, they would have immediately noticed the telltale signs; it was later claimed that a small dose of quinine would have saved his life.
几十年前，他们本会立即注意到这些迹象；后来有人声称，一小剂奎宁本来可以救他一命。

paragraphs.brief: 此外，这本书令人信服地指出，该疾病是“现代意大利历史大图中不可分割的一部分”。
sentences: As there are still more than 1m deaths every year from malaria worldwide, Snowden’s book also has contemporary relevance.
由于全世界每年仍有超过100万人死于疟疾，斯诺登的书也具有当代意义。
This is a disease that affects every level of the societies where it is rampant.
这是一种疾病，影响到其肆虐的社会各阶层。
The economic miracle of the 1950s and 1960s which made Italy into a modern industrial nation would not have been possible without the eradication of malaria.
1950年代和1960年代的经济奇迹使意大利成为一个现代工业国家，没有消灭疟疾就不可能实现。
Moreover, this book convincingly argues that the disease was ‘an integral part of the big picture of modern Italian history’.
此外，这本书令人信服地指出，该疾病是“现代意大利历史大图中不可分割的一部分”。
This magnificent study, beautifully written and impeccably documented, deserves an audience beyond specialists in history, or in Italy.
这份出色的研究写得漂亮记录得无可挑剔值得在历史上或在意大利成为专家以外的观众

items.en: a figure showing the dramatic results of an anti-malarial drug programme
items.zh: a 表明抗疟疾药物方案取得巨大成果的数字。
items.why: E段用死亡人数在二十世纪头十年下降约八成来说明药物计划的显著效果。

items.en: an important discovery about how malaria is spread
items.why: C段记述格拉西确认传播疟疾病原体的是蚊虫，构成有关传播途径的突破。

items.en: mention of an expert’s decision not to halt the spread of the disease
items.zh: 专家决定不阻止该疾病的传播
items.why: 疟疾专家米西罗利拒绝下令发放奎宁，文中明确说结果让疫情不受控制地扩散。

items.en: the significance of the malaria story for today’s readers
items.zh: 疟疾故事对今日读者的意义
items.why: H段把当时全球仍有大量疟疾死亡与这本书联系，说明历史研究对当代读者的意义。

items.en: examples of false assumptions which held back scientific understanding of malaria
items.zh: 妨碍科学了解疟疾的虚假假设的例子
items.why: B段举出疟疾被误认为可以遗传、疫情被归咎于意大利炎热地区来者等错误认识。

items.en: a reference to legislation to support the fight against malaria
items.zh: 提及支持防治疟疾的立法
items.why: D段给出具体立法，在1904年出台奎宁法并设置奎宁税，以支持发药防治疟疾。

items.en: Malaria in 19th-century Italy Up until the late nineteenth century, experts failed to make the connection between malaria and ________.
items.zh: 直到 19 世纪晚期，专家一直未能把疟疾与________联系起来。
items.why: 回到对应内容“另一些则在沼泽地、水和疟疾之间建立联系，但没有进一步向昆虫过渡”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The most popular belief at the time was the ________ theory, which upheld the idea that diseases were carried by unclean air.
items.zh: 当时最流行的是________理论，认为疾病通过不洁的空气传播。
items.why: 回到对应内容“但19世纪，大多数专家都赞同“弥撒”或“毒气”理论”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Another common idea was that malaria was a ________ disease, and as a result people from certain parts of the country were often held responsible for the spread of epidemics.
items.zh: 另一种普遍的看法是，疟疾是一种________疾病。因此，来自某些地区的人常被指责为疫情的传播者。
items.why: 段B 倒数第 2 句:“…given the widespread belief that malaria was hereditary.”一一疙疾被误认为是遗传病。

items.en: Malaria was particularly widespread in rural regions, where ________ could be extremely short.
items.zh: 疟疾在农村尤其普遍，当地的________有时短得惊人。
items.why: 回到对应内容“在温暖、潮湿、疟疾地区，土地工人的预期寿命是可怕的22.5岁”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词。

items.en: The volunteers in Giovanni Battista Grassi’s research came from all parts of Italy.
items.zh: Giovanni Battista Grassi研究的志愿者来自意大利各地。
items.why: 段 C 只提到“healthy human volunteers”,并未说明这些志愿者“来自意大利各地”。故信息缺失。

items.en: Experiments in Italy proved that it was possible to remain healthy despite being in malarial zones.
items.zh: 在意大利进行的实验证明，尽管在疟疾地区，但仍有可能保持健康。
items.why: 实验让健康人住进疟区，同时避免蚊虫叮咬，他们仍保持健康，证明身处疟区未必发病。

items.en: In the early twentieth century, quinine was successfully administered to all inhabitants of vulnerable regions.
items.zh: 在二十世纪初，奎宁成功地为脆弱地区的所有居民管理。
items.why: 段 E 首句指出原本打算向所有易感地区居民发放奎宁,“peasants were often suspicious of medicine…refusal to accept the treatment”,并未做到“成功地给所有居民服用”。

points: C段记述格拉西确认传播疟疾病原体的是蚊虫，构成有关传播途径的突破。
段 C 只提到“healthy human volunteers”,并未说明这些志愿者“来自意大利各地”。故信息缺失。
clauses: “that malaria is carried by mosquitoes”补足 knows 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 knows 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
“that affects every level of the societies where it is rampant”修饰前面的 disease。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 disease，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: A review of Frank M Snowden’s masterly history of a country’s fight to eradicate a deadly disease
Frank M Snowden关于国家消灭致命疾病斗争的伟大历史回顾
